purpose: Human-reviewable scale plan consumed by Scripts/release_scale_keilim.py. Rescales the three Heikhal vessel studies in the combined map to the dimensions given in Lishchno Tidreshu (book review item 8). Every number below was resolved from receipts on disk; nothing here is a claim of visual acceptance or of a measured Temple Institute replica.

units.unitStatus: Existing reconstruction convention (50 cm amah, 6 tefachim per amah); not a claim that all halachic measures agree. The golden altar uses the book's 5-tefach amah (p. 255) = 41.667 cm.

frame: X east, Y south, Z up. Heikhal clear floor X -5600..-3600, Y -500..+500, floor top Z 925 (measured SM_0146_floor_Heichal_clear_floor).

wallClearance.measure: world AABB of the whole actor (branch tips included for the menorah) to the Y=-500 and Y=+500 walls
wallClearance.rule: A group whose predicted post-scale AABB is closer than minCm to either north/south wall is OMITTED (recorded with numeric evidence) and nothing is scaled or moved for it. Other groups proceed. Override the threshold with -KeilimWallClearanceCm=<cm> on the engine command line.
wallClearance.knownState: The menorah at Y=+350 (keilim-move-20260907T163327Z) already has its branch tips 79.25 cm from the south wall; after the 5/6 scale the tips sit at Y 408.96 (91.04 cm) and the base edge at Y 387.5 (112.5 cm). With the default 100 cm the menorah is therefore omitted; pass -KeilimWallClearanceCm=90 to accept 91 cm, or move the menorah to Y about +315 (book review reading A, 2.5 amot to the branch tips) before scaling.

identification.rule: Same as run-release-move-keilim.py: static-mesh actors inside the Heikhal floor rectangle are clustered by current XY; each cluster must contain exactly one actor and its label must equal the expected label; the static mesh path, pre-scale bounds (tolerance boundsToleranceCm) and current scale (1,1,1) must match. An actor already at the target scale is recorded as already_scaled and skipped.

menorah.label: REVIEW_TempleInstituteMenorahStudyV1
menorah.yawMeaning: Local X spans the seven lamps; yaw 90 puts the branches north-south (Rambam Beit HaBechirah 3:12; book pp. 252-254). Uniform scaling leaves the rotation untouched; the script verifies yaw before and after.
menorah.pivot: origin at the base contact plane (local Z min = 0); scaling about the actor location keeps the base on the floor

currentDimensionsCm.note: World X = local Y (depth), world Y = local X (lamp span) because of yaw 90. Base footprint (BaseLower part) 90 x 78 cm local.

menorah.scaleDerivation: 150 / 180 = 5/6. 18 tefachim x 8.3333 cm = 150 cm at this project's 50 cm amah. The model's 180 cm was the Temple Institute schematic conversion at a larger amah (menorah-model-spec.json physical_dimensions.warning).

book.quote: The height of the Menorah is eighteen tefachim (1), and before the Menorah there is a stone with three steps, upon which the Kohen stands
book.alternatives: None recorded in the book for the height. The Temple Institute's 180 cm is the same 18 tefachim at a 60 cm amah (10 cm tefach); the project convention is 50 cm.

shulchan.enabledByDefaultReason: Non-uniform Z scaling is a judgment call: it doubles the tabletop slab thickness, the tefach frame (8.33 -> 16.67 cm) and the crown height while leaving leg cross-sections unchanged. Uniform scaling to 150 cm high would make the footprint 200 x 100 cm (4 x 2 amot) and break the book's 2 x 1 amot. Enable with -KeilimGroups=shulchan (or together with the others) after deciding, or treat the height as a modelling task.
shulchan.label: REVIEW_HeikhalKeilim_SM_ShulchanStudy
shulchan.yawMeaning: Yaw 0 keeps the 100 cm long axis east-west ('its length along the length of the House', book p. 250).
shulchan.localBoundsSource: SourceAssets/vessels-review/HeikhalKeilimV1/geometry-manifest.json (tabletop 100 x 50, rings add 1.5 cm each side in Y, tabletop at 75, crown top at 76)
shulchan.pivot: origin at the base contact plane (local Z min = 0)

currentDimensionsCm.note: Footprint already 2 x 1 amot (100 x 50 body; 53 with rings). Height to tabletop 75 cm = 1.5 amot (Shemos 25:23 convention used by heikhal-keilim-spec.json).

shulchan.scaleDerivation: Tabletop 75 -> 150 cm (3 amot): Z scale 2.0; crown top lands at 152 cm. Alternative 150/76 = 1.9737 puts the crown top at exactly 150 cm (tabletop 148.4). Footprint unchanged, so the north-wall clearance stays 123.5 cm.
shulchan.uniformAlternativeRejected: Uniform 2.0 would give bounds X -5400..-5200, Y -456..-244 (footprint 200 x 106 cm, north clearance 44 cm) and violate the 2 x 1 amot footprint the book states on the same page.

book.quote: The length of the shulchan is two amos, in width one amah, and in height three amos [Yechezkel 41:22]
book.bookSource: Yechezkel 41:22; the 3-amah height is the author's main line (Targum, Rashi, Radak, Metzudos, Mishkenei Elyon), book pp. 241-249
book.alternatives: p. 246 (Tosafos Menachos 97a): the three amot may include the lechem hapanim stacked on the table, in which case the table body stays 1.5 amot (75 cm) and no rescale is due; the bread would then be modelled 75 cm tall above the tabletop.

altar.label: REVIEW_HeikhalKeilim_SM_GoldenIncenseAltarStudy
altar.localBoundsSource: SourceAssets/vessels-review/HeikhalKeilimV1/geometry-manifest.json (body 50 x 50, rings add 1.5 cm each side in Y, horn tops at 100, body top at 90)
altar.pivot: origin at the base contact plane (local Z min = 0)

currentDimensionsCm.note: 1 x 1 amah body, 2 amot high at the 6-tefach 50 cm amah.

targetDimensionsCm.note: Body; rings make the world Y AABB 44.17 cm.

book.quote: one amah by one amah in length and width and two amos in height, and every amah is measured by an amah of five tefachim
book.bookSource: Shemos 30:2; Rambam Beit HaBechirah 3:17; note 4: Eruvin 4a per Yechezkel 43:13 (also p. 253)
book.alternatives: None recorded in the book. The 5-tefach amah applies to the golden altar only; the shulchan and menorah keep the 6-tefach amah.
